To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-terminal domain of HCF is necessary for the interaction between N- and C-termini of HCF and that the kelch repeats of HCF are sufficient for complex formation with VP16.
the C-terminal region of host cell factor (residues C-terminal to the kelch repeats) is required for VP16 complex and HCF self-interaction, whereas the N-terminal region is required for VP6 binding.

the kelch repeats of HCF are sufficient for VP16 binding, that the C terminus of HCF is sufficient for N-terminal binding, and that the C terminally located residues of HCF that interfere with VP16 binding are required for N-terminal binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the domains of host cell factor (hcf) involved in VP6 complex formation and in hcf self-association.
the molecular basis of the interaction of the VP16 transactivator with the host cell factor HCF.
the identification and characterization of the host cell factors that are required for the activation of transcription by herpes simplex virus type 1 immediate early protein, VP16.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-terminal region of HFC is sufficient for interaction of HCF with VP16, but that the C-terminal region is required for the association between the two domains of HCF.
VP16 binds to the N- and the C-terminal regions of the HCF protein and that the N-terminal region of HFC binds to the C-terminal region of the HFC protein.
the N terminus of HCF is sufficient for the VP16 interaction, but not sufficient for HCF dimerization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the VP16 complex formation domain of HCF is contained within the first 380 residues of the protein, but that the C-terminal region of the molecule, including residues 381–450, is necessary to allow interaction between the N-terminal and C-terminal regions.

VP16 binds to HCF through the kelch repeats, that this interaction is stabilized by the C terminus of HCF, and that the N- and the C-terminal regions of the protein are required to form an active HCF molecule.
the C-terminal region of VP16 interacts with the kelch domain of HCF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N-terminal and C-terminal regions are not sufficient for VP16 interaction.
the C-terminal region of the protein is important for VP16 binding, but is also necessary for the interaction between HCF’s N- and C-termini.
HCF has multiple roles in VP16 complex assembly, and that these roles are separable.
